definition: Password hashing stores a slow, salted hash of a password instead of the password. A slow function, such as Argon2, bcrypt, or scrypt, makes guessing expensive. A fast hash such as plain SHA-256 is the wrong tool, because guesses can be checked too quickly.
details: The salt is stored beside the hash. Verification hashes the submitted password with the same salt and compares the results.
examples: A user table that stores a hash and a salt, not a password
